title: Set-valued models of a small finite-limit sketch
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ as in [def-weil-size-convention]. A finite-limit sketch consists of a $\mathcal U$-small category $\mathcal A$ and a $\mathcal U$-small family of specified cones in $\mathcal A$, each over a finite diagram (finite means finitely many objects and morphisms, as in [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]). A model is a functor $M:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Set}_{\mathcal U}$ taking every specified cone to a limit cone; morphisms of models are natural transformations. Write $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal A)$ for the full subcategory of the functor category consisting of these models, formed in $\mathcal V$. Then $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal A)$ has $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets and all $\mathcal U$-small limits and colimits. Limits and filtered colimits are computed pointwise in $\operatorname{Set}_{\mathcal U}$. Here filtered and colimit have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Moreover there is a $\mathcal U$-small family of models such that every model is a $\mathcal U$-small filtered colimit of members of that family and the ordinary Hom functor from each member preserves $\mathcal U$-small filtered colimits. Thus the category of models is locally finitely presentable relative to $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Adamek-Rosicky, Locally Presentable and Accessible Categories (1994), Chapter 1, Corollary 1.52 (finite-limit sketches), together with completeness and pointwise limits/filtered colimits of models. Publisher chapter synopsis read online; full chapter not locally archived, WANTED in report. No corresponding Stacks tag identified.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\operatorname{Set}_{\mathcal U})$. By [lem-coef-presheaf-local-finite-presentability], applied to $C=\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$, this is locally finitely presentable. Its Hom sets are $\mathcal U$-small: a natural transformation is a family in $\prod_{a\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal A}\operatorname{Set}(F(a),G(a))$ satisfying the naturality equations, hence a subset of a $\mathcal U$-small product.

source.place: Agent construction of the finite-sketch comparison arrows, followed by the cardinal-specific orthogonality theorem at lines 472-479; see also the source places in the cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: For later use, the pointwise constructions in $\mathcal P$ follow directly from sets. For any $\mathcal U$-small diagram $(F_i)_{i\in I}$, its limit at $a$ is the set of compatible tuples in $\prod_i F_i(a)$, with arrows of $\mathcal A$ acting componentwise; any cone factors uniquely by its component maps. Its colimit at $a$ is the quotient of $\coprod_i F_i(a)$ by the equivalence relation generated by $(i,x)\sim(j,F_\alpha(a)x)$ for every $\alpha:i\to j$; arrows of $\mathcal A$ act on representatives and respect these relations by naturality. A cocone induces a unique map on this quotient. These component maps are natural by their formulas, giving the functor-category universal properties. Both constructions stay in $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Agent construction of the finite-sketch comparison arrows, followed by the cardinal-specific orthogonality theorem at lines 472-479; see also the source places in the cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: For $a\in\mathcal A$ write $h_a=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(a,-)$. A specified cone has apex $a$ and legs $a\to D(j)$ for a finite category $J$ and a functor $D:J\to\mathcal A$. The legs induce a cocone from $j\mapsto h_{D(j)}$, indexed by $J^{\mathrm{op}}$, to $h_a$. Form $Q_D=\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}h_{D(j)}$ by Step 2 and its induced arrow $s_D:Q_D\to h_a$. Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], on $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the colimit universal property give $\operatorname{Hom}(h_a,M)=M(a)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(Q_D,M)=\lim_{j\in J}M(D(j))$. Indeed a map from $Q_D$ is exactly a compatible family of maps from the $h_{D(j)}$, which Yoneda identifies with a compatible family of elements. Its naturality formula identifies precomposition with $s_D$ with the given cone comparison map. Thus $M$ is a model exactly when it is orthogonal to every $s_D$.

source.place: Agent construction of the finite-sketch comparison arrows, followed by the cardinal-specific orthogonality theorem at lines 472-479; see also the source places in the cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: Each $h_a$ is finitely presentable: by Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], its Hom functor is evaluation at $a$, which preserves filtered colimits by Step 2. Each $Q_D$ is finitely presentable as well: for a small filtered diagram $(F_i)$ the preceding Hom identification and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] give $\operatorname{Hom}(Q_D,\operatorname{colim}_iF_i)=\lim_j\operatorname{colim}_iF_i(D(j))=\operatorname{colim}_i\lim_jF_i(D(j))=\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(Q_D,F_i)$. This is the canonical map because every identification is induced by the evaluation projections and colimit coprojections. The theorem applies since $J$ has finitely many objects and morphisms and $I$ is small filtered. The family $S=\{s_D\}$ is $\mathcal U$-small, being indexed by the given small family of cones. Thus both endpoints of every arrow in $S$ are finitely presentable.

source.place: Agent construction of the finite-sketch comparison arrows, followed by the cardinal-specific orthogonality theorem at lines 472-479; see also the source places in the cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-finite-orthogonality-presentability] to $\mathcal C=\mathcal P$ and this $S$. Step 1 verifies the locally finite presentability and Hom-size hypotheses, and Step 4 verifies smallness and finite presentability of both endpoints. Step 3 identifies the resulting full orthogonality subcategory, including its natural-transformation morphisms, with the model category itself. Consequently the models have all $\mathcal U$-small colimits and a $\mathcal U$-small family of finitely presentable models generating every model under $\mathcal U$-small filtered colimits. This is exactly the required Hom-preservation and generation clause.

source.place: Agent construction of the finite-sketch comparison arrows, followed by the cardinal-specific orthogonality theorem at lines 472-479; see also the source places in the cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: For any small diagram $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ of models, let $L$ be its pointwise limit from Step 2. For each specified cone $(a\to D(j))$, $L(a)=\lim_i M_i(a)=\lim_i\lim_j M_i(D(j))=\lim_j\lim_i M_i(D(j))=\lim_jL(D(j))$. The interchange sends a compatible family $(x_{i,j})$ to the same family with the two indices reordered: compatibility in both indices is precisely the same equations. This proves the comparison is bijective, also when $I$ or $J$ is empty. Thus $L$ is a model; the ambient universal property remains a universal property in the full model subcategory. It gives all small limits computed pointwise. Hom sets remain small as subsets of the natural-transformation sets of Step 1.

source.place: Agent construction of the finite-sketch comparison arrows, followed by the cardinal-specific orthogonality theorem at lines 472-479; see also the source places in the cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: For a $\mathcal U$-small filtered diagram $(M_i)$ of models, form its pointwise colimit $N$ as in Step 2. At every specified finite cone, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] makes the canonical comparison $N(a)=\operatorname{colim}_i M_i(a)=\operatorname{colim}_i\lim_j M_i(D(j))\to\lim_j\operatorname{colim}_iM_i(D(j))=\lim_jN(D(j))$ a bijection. Hence $N$ is a model. Its cocone is already universal among all functors, so is universal among the models, which form a full subcategory. This proves pointwise computation of filtered colimits, including the condition at specified empty cones because filtered categories are nonempty.
